name: Approval Chance Predictor
description: Get a realistic percentage chance of approval before you submit a verification application, based on the same details reviewers use to reject applications. Built for businesses applying for verification and for agencies managing many client applications at once.

config.prompt: Compare this business against the most common reasons Meta/Google verification applications get rejected (mismatched business details, missing privacy policy, unverifiable address, inconsistent documents). Business: {{input.businessName}}, address {{input.address}}, website {{input.website}}. Existing readiness data: {{input.record}}. List every risk factor found, one per line starting with "RISK:".

config.message:
:bar_chart: Approval prediction for *{{input.businessName}}*: {{input.approvalPercentage}}% likely to pass.
Risks: {{input.risks}}

config.body:

name: Business Details Matcher
description: Catches the silent rejection cause: a business name or address that's written slightly differently on the website vs. the GST filing vs. the bank account. (No instant Airtable-update trigger exists yet, so this polls on a schedule instead of firing immediately.)

config.prompt: Extract the business name, address, and phone number as they appear on the website HTML: {{input.body}}. Then extract the same three fields from each uploaded document for this client: {{input.newlyReady}}. Return each version clearly labeled by source (Website, GST, PAN, Bank Statement).

config.body:
Here's what matches and what doesn't across your website, GST, PAN, and bank statement:

{{input.mismatches}}
config.subject: Business details check for {{input.businessName}}

name: Client Priority Ranker

config.prompt: For each client in this list: {{input.records}}, estimate how likely they are to succeed vs. need help, based on their delay history, issue count, and past outcomes. For each client, output a line: "ClientName | needsHelp: true/false | priority: 1-10".

config.message:
:clipboard: This week's client priority ranking (highest priority first):
{{input.ranked}}

name: Cross-Platform Sync Engine
description: Keep client data in Airtable, your CRM, and a shared spreadsheet from drifting apart. This workflow polls for changes, figures out exactly which fields moved so nothing gets oversynced, and pushes just those updates out to HubSpot and Google Sheets, with a quiet Slack log for troubleshooting. (No instant Airtable-update trigger exists yet, so this polls every 15 minutes instead of firing immediately.)

config.message: :white_check_mark: Synced {{input.changed.length}} changed client record(s) to HubSpot and Google Sheets.

name: Customer Support Agent
description: Intelligent customer support agent that handles FAQs, checks order status, and escalates complex issues to human agents. Fully working with intent detection, data fetching, and confidence-based routing.

config.code: const query = (input.message || input.query || '').toLowerCase(); const orderKeywords = ['order', 'status', 'tracking', 'shipment', 'delivery', 'when will', 'where is']; const complaintKeywords = ['complaint', 'problem', 'issue', 'wrong', 'broken', 'refund', 'cancel']; const faqKeywords = ['what', 'how', 'why', 'when', 'where', 'can i', 'do you']; let intent = 'faq'; let confidence = 0.7; if (orderKeywords.some(kw => query.includes(kw))) { intent = 'order'; confidence = 0.85; } else if (complaintKeywords.some(kw => query.includes(kw))) { intent = 'complaint'; confidence = 0.9; } else if (faqKeywords.some(kw => query.includes(kw))) { intent = 'faq'; confidence = 0.8; } return { intent, confidence, originalQuery: input.message || input.query, orderId: query.match(/order[\s#]*([A-Z0-9-]+)/i)?.[1] || null };

const order = input.data && input.data[0]; if (!order) { return { found: false, message: 'Order not found' }; } return { found: true, orderStatus: order.status || 'Unknown', orderDate: order.created_at || 'Unknown', estimatedDelivery: order.estimated_delivery || 'Not available', items: order.items || [] };

config.prompt: You are a helpful customer support agent. The user asked about their order. Order details: Status: {{input.orderStatus}}, Order Date: {{input.orderDate}}, Estimated Delivery: {{input.estimatedDelivery}}. User query: {{input.originalQuery}}. Provide a clear, friendly response about their order status. If order not found, apologize and ask them to verify their order ID.

You are a helpful customer support agent. A customer has a complaint. User query: {{input.originalQuery}}. Acknowledge their concern, apologize if appropriate, and explain that you will help resolve this. Be empathetic and professional.

You are a helpful customer support agent. Answer the following question clearly and concisely: {{input.originalQuery}}. If you do not know the answer, politely say so and offer to connect them with a human agent.

config.message: Escalated to human agent. Ticket created.

name: FAQ Answering Assistant
description: Let clients ask their own questions instead of pinging your team every time. This chat assistant answers strictly from your own FAQ records and automatically hands the question to a human in Slack whenever it isn't confident in the answer.

config.prompt: You are a support assistant. Using ONLY the information in these FAQ records: {{input.records}}, answer this client question: "{{input.message}}". If the FAQ records do not contain a confident answer, say "I am not fully sure" and set your confidence low. Respond with a JSON object: {"answer": "...", "confidence": 0.0-1.0}.

name: Finance / Compliance Agent
description: Automated finance operations agent that processes invoices and expenses, categorizes transactions, performs compliance checks, and triggers alerts for anomalies. Reduces manual finance workload.

config.code: return { type: input.type || input.transaction_type || 'expense', amount: parseFloat(input.amount || 0), vendor: input.vendor || input.supplier || '', description: input.description || input.notes || '', date: input.date || input.transaction_date || new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0], category: input.category || '', invoice_number: input.invoice_number || input.invoice_id || '', employee_id: input.employee_id || input.employee || '', receipt_url: input.receipt_url || input.file_url || '', timestamp: new Date().toISOString() };

config.prompt: Categorize this financial transaction. Return JSON: { category: string (one of: Travel, Meals, Software, Hardware, Office Supplies, Marketing, Professional Services, Utilities, Other), confidence: number (0-1), reasoning: string }\n\nTransaction: Vendor: {{input.vendor}}, Description: {{input.description}}, Amount: ${{input.amount}}

config.code: try { const content = input.content || input.text || input.response || '{}'; const jsonMatch = content.match(/\{[\s\S]*\}/); if (jsonMatch) { const parsed = JSON.parse(jsonMatch[0]); return { category: parsed.category || 'Other', confidence: parsed.confidence || 0.5, reasoning: parsed.reasoning || 'No reasoning', transaction: input }; } return { category: 'Other', confidence: 0.5, reasoning: 'Could not parse', transaction: input }; } catch (e) { return { category: 'Other', confidence: 0.5, reasoning: 'Error: ' + e.message, transaction: input }; }

const amount = parseFloat(input.transaction.amount || 0); const category = input.category; const violations = []; if (amount > 10000) { violations.push({ type: 'high_amount', message: 'Transaction exceeds $10,000 - requires approval' }); } if (amount < 0) { violations.push({ type: 'negative_amount', message: 'Negative amount detected - possible refund or error' }); } if (!category || category === 'Other') { violations.push({ type: 'uncategorized', message: 'Transaction is uncategorized - needs review' }); } if (!input.transaction.vendor || input.transaction.vendor.trim() === '') { violations.push({ type: 'missing_vendor', message: 'Missing vendor information' }); } return { compliant: violations.length === 0, violations, transaction: input.transaction, category: input.category, confidence: input.confidence };

name: HR / Hiring Workflow Agent
description: Automated resume processing agent that extracts skills, matches candidates against job requirements, scores applications, and automatically schedules interviews for shortlisted candidates.

config.code: return { name: input.name || input.candidate_name || 'Unknown', email: input.email || input.candidate_email || '', resume_text: input.resume_text || input.resume || input.text || '', job_role: input.job_role || input.position || '', resume_file_url: input.resume_file_url || input.file_url || '', timestamp: new Date().toISOString() };

config.prompt: Extract skills, experience, education, and qualifications from this resume. Return a JSON object: { skills: ["skill1", "skill2"], experience_years: number, education: string, certifications: ["cert1"], summary: string }\n\nResume text: {{input.resume_text}}

config.code: try { const content = input.content || input.text || input.response || '{}'; const jsonMatch = content.match(/\{[\s\S]*\}/); if (jsonMatch) { const parsed = JSON.parse(jsonMatch[0]); return { skills: parsed.skills || [], experience_years: parsed.experience_years || 0, education: parsed.education || '', certifications: parsed.certifications || [], summary: parsed.summary || '', originalData: input }; } return { skills: [], experience_years: 0, education: '', certifications: [], summary: '', originalData: input }; } catch (e) { return { skills: [], experience_years: 0, education: '', certifications: [], summary: '', originalData: input }; }

config.prompt: Match this candidate against the job role: {{input.job_role}}. Candidate skills: {{input.skills}}, Experience: {{input.experience_years}} years, Education: {{input.education}}. Return JSON: { match_score: number (0-100), shortlisted: boolean (score >= 70), strengths: ["strength1"], gaps: ["gap1"], recommendation: string }

config.code: try { const content = input.content || input.text || input.response || '{}'; const jsonMatch = content.match(/\{[\s\S]*\}/); if (jsonMatch) { const parsed = JSON.parse(jsonMatch[0]); return { match_score: parsed.match_score || 0, shortlisted: parsed.shortlisted !== undefined ? parsed.shortlisted : (parsed.match_score >= 70), strengths: parsed.strengths || [], gaps: parsed.gaps || [], recommendation: parsed.recommendation || 'No recommendation', candidateData: input.originalData }; } return { match_score: 0, shortlisted: false, strengths: [], gaps: [], recommendation: 'Could not parse match result', candidateData: input.originalData }; } catch (e) { return { match_score: 0, shortlisted: false, strengths: [], gaps: [], recommendation: 'Error: ' + e.message, candidateData: input.originalData }; }

const baseUrl = 'https://calendly.com/hr-team/interview'; const params = new URLSearchParams({ name: input.candidateData.name, email: input.candidateData.email, job: input.candidateData.job_role }); return { calendarLink: `${baseUrl}?${params.toString()}`, email: input.candidateData.email, name: input.candidateData.name, jobRole: input.candidateData.job_role };

name: Missing Document Finder
description: Stop chasing clients for 'one more document.' Upload whatever paperwork a client has sent so far, in any order, and this workflow figures out exactly which required documents are still missing and messages the client a specific checklist on WhatsApp.

config.formDescription: Upload whatever documents you have — in any order. We will tell you what is still missing.

name: Smart Alert Co-Pilot
description: Move from 'checking on a schedule' to 'getting told the moment something's wrong.' An AI judgment layer watches your client records, pulls related context before deciding, and sends a targeted alert to the right person only when a change is actually worth interrupting someone for. (No instant Airtable-update trigger exists yet, so this polls every 10 minutes instead of firing immediately.)

config.systemPrompt: You are a compliance monitoring co-pilot. You are given a changed client record plus related context records. Decide whether this change is worth interrupting a person for right now (e.g. a readiness score dropped sharply, a document expired, a risk flag appeared) versus routine (e.g. a timestamp update, a minor note edit). Reply as JSON: {"alertWorthy": true/false, "reason": "...", "severity": "low|medium|high"}.

name: Submission Package Builder
description: Once a client's readiness score clears the bar, this workflow automatically gathers the homepage/policy screenshots, live policy text, and already-uploaded documents a verification submission needs, and emails you all the pieces. Simplification: since this platform has no PDF-merge node, the pieces are delivered as individual links rather than one combined PDF.

config.subject: Submission package ready for {{input.businessName}}

name: Verification Co-Pilot Chat
description: Answer 'what's the status of X?' without anyone manually digging through records. Ask in plain English over WhatsApp or Slack and an AI co-pilot pulls the live client record — and optionally a platform status API — to give a grounded, current answer, with no app-switching required.

config.systemPrompt: You are the Verification Co-Pilot. You never guess — you only answer using the client record and status data given to you below. If the data does not cover the question, say so plainly and offer to escalate to a human.

name: Verification Readiness Checker
description: Know whether your business will pass Meta or Google verification before you apply. This workflow scores your website and documents against the checks verifiers actually run — privacy policy, terms, matching business details — then emails and WhatsApps you a fix list so you can pass on the first try.

config.successMessage: Thanks! We are analyzing your business now.
config.formDescription: Tell us about your business so we can check your verification readiness.

config.prompt: You are a compliance analyst preparing a business for Meta/Google verification. Website HTML: {{input.body}}. Business name on file: {{input.businessName}}. Uploaded documents: GST {{input.gstDocument}}, PAN {{input.panDocument}}, bank statement {{input.bankStatement}}. Check for: a visible Privacy Policy page, a visible Terms & Conditions page, a business name and address that match across the website and the documents, and a working contact page. List every issue you find as one line starting with "ISSUE:". If everything looks correct, return "NO ISSUES FOUND".

Based on these readiness issues: {{input.issues}}, write 2-3 short, plain-English fixes the client should make before applying for Meta/Google verification. Keep it friendly, specific, and actionable. No jargon.

config.body:
Hi {{input.businessName}},

Your verification readiness score is {{input.score}}/100.

Here is what to fix before you apply:
{{input.fixList}}

We will keep this record on file for your next check.
config.subject: Your verification readiness score: {{input.score}}/100

config.text: Hi {{input.businessName}}! Your verification readiness score is {{input.score}}/100. Check your email for the full fix list, or reply here with questions.
